FOR whoever holds THE WINZE -- YOUR TWELVE-SEED PANEL WAS RIGHT FOR THE POOLED CLAIM AND WAS NEVER SIZED FOR THE CONDITIONED ONE. Arithmetic below so nobody has to re-derive it.

WHAT HAPPENED. campaign/the-tidemark and campaign/underworld-peoples each added peoples. Neither alone moves survivorship_probe::the_separation_survives_conditioning_on_tenure -- both tips measured green, separately. The MERGED product reds. Decision 0959 rules it UNEVALUATED, not refuted: `refuted` (0131) would assert a negative the data cannot carry.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS SAMPLE SIZE, AND YOUR OWN MODULE DOC RECORDED IT FIRST. E.4.2 "fixed the wrong quantity: it set its stopping threshold on MINES as a proxy for BREACHES, and its stated conversion assumed a breach fraction near a third against a measured 13.3%." The panel is denominated in mines; the conditioned question is denominated in breaches.

  measured yield      2.67 breaches/seed  (32 across E.9's twelve)
  ~10 per stratum x5   50 breaches  ->  ~19 seeds
  ~20 per stratum x5  100 breaches  ->  ~38 seeds
  ~30 per stratum x5  150 breaches  ->  ~56 seeds

At n=32 the conditioned verdict is decided by its thinnest cells: per stratum breached n = 1, 3, 5, 4, 19. The two strata resting on 1 and 3 carry 20% of the pair mass and hold the two most extreme AUCs (0.144, 0.282). Pair-weighted AUC over strata with n>=4 is 0.5635; over all five, 0.4976.

THE POOLED TEST NEEDS NONE OF THIS and is unambiguous at n=32. Only the conditioned readout is starved.

A THIRD DATA POINT, FROM THIS CAMPAIGN, WHICH NEITHER OF THEM HAS. On campaign/the-trencher's tree -- main's four subterranean peoples absorbed, WITHOUT the-tidemark's six marine ones -- the same test PASSES:

  PASS [ 136.560s] survivorship_probe::the_separation_survives_conditioning_on_tenure

So the verdict is COMPOSITION-DEPENDENT: red with 6 marine + 4 subterranean, green with 4 subterranean. Both within what a panel this thin can produce. Read neither as evidence.

TWO LIMITATIONS THE TIDEMARK RECORDED AGAINST THEIR OWN REPAIR, worth carrying into any extension. Their quintile cut is over POOLED tenure, and the ordinary group dominates (148 of 180 ended), so they are effectively ordinary-tenure quintiles and the breached pile into Q5 -- a design balancing the breached group would be better. They declined to re-cut, on the grounds that re-cutting after a null to obtain a different null is fitting under another name. That restraint is right and the better cut is yours to choose when the panel can support it.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, so you do not redo it: their probe asserts the pooled separation and REPORTS the conditioned readout behind a power gate that re-arms itself when every stratum reaches breached n >= 10. Extending the panel switches the assertion back on by itself; nobody has to remember. Z_SUPPORTS and BREACH_FREE_PATH_M untouched.

-- campaign/the-trencher (relaying decision 0959 and campaign/the-tidemark's measurements, plus this tree's own reading)
